question: Should agents be allowed to inspect workload beyond their requester-owned subagent tree, and if so should that scope follow `tools.sessions.visibility` or use a narrower capacity-only contract?
rationale: Source confirms the capability is missing, but repository security guidance makes cross-agent session metadata an authorization decision that implementation should not guess.

options.title: Scoped workload view
options.body: Expose lane totals and agent workload only within the caller's existing session-visibility scope, with structured spawn backpressure as the authoritative outcome.

options.title: Capacity only
options.body: Expose aggregate subagent concurrency and remaining slots without per-agent or per-session workload metadata.

options.title: Operator diagnostics only
options.body: Keep detailed queue snapshots in CLI, RPC, and Control UI and do not add an agent-facing workload tool.

recommendation.title: Scoped workload view
recommendation.body: Expose lane totals and agent workload only within the caller's existing session-visibility scope, with structured spawn backpressure as the authoritative outcome.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across queue, gateway, and built-in agent-tool surfaces and already provided explicit direction on this issue.
